## Description

**What**: Create bug-classification-stats.sh and integrate it as a mandatory step in /dso:retro SKILL.md.
**Why**: SC5 closes the feedback loop — the registry and classifier write data, the retro step surfaces patterns. Without this, the classification system accumulates data silently with no operational impact.
**Scope**:
- IN: plugins/dso/scripts/bug-classification-stats.sh; /dso:retro SKILL.md modifications for mandatory classification step; config keys bug_classification.recurrence_threshold (default 3) and bug_classification.retro_window_days (default 60)
- OUT: The classifier agent (S2), backfill (S3), retro visualization or dashboards (out of epic scope)

## Done Definitions

- When this story is complete, plugins/dso/scripts/bug-classification-stats.sh exists, accepts --window-days N parameter, uses .claude/scripts/dso ticket list (excludes deleted tickets), and aggregates bug-type-* tags; consumes the machine-readable slug list from S1's registry export (does not re-parse the markdown directly)
  <- Satisfies: "SC5: Calls bug-classification-stats.sh --window-days <bug_classification.retro_window_days>"
- When this story is complete, /dso:retro SKILL.md contains a MANDATORY Bug Classification step that invokes bug-classification-stats.sh and surfaces EACH of the following as a distinct, explicitly-labeled finding when its trigger fires (MUST NOT merge or inline into general retro prose): (a) bug-type-uncategorized count >= recurrence_threshold: labeled finding; (b) any registry slug count >= recurrence_threshold: labeled finding; (c) ANY bug-type-classifier-failed-* tag present (threshold fixed at 1): labeled finding
  <- Satisfies: "SC5: MUST surface EACH as distinct explicitly-labeled finding"
- When this story is complete, when no trigger fires, /dso:retro MUST emit the exact text: "Bug classification health: no threshold breaches in this window." (silence is not acceptable)
  <- Satisfies: "SC5: MUST emit explicit positive confirmation when no triggers fire"
- When this story is complete, the dual-count semantics of classifier-failed-* vs uncategorized are documented in bug-classification-stats.sh: a ticket that carries both bug-type-uncategorized AND bug-type-classifier-failed-<reason> is counted in the uncategorized counter OR the classifier-failed counter (not both), with the chosen deduplication approach stated explicitly in the script comments
  <- Satisfies: adversarial finding on dual-count ambiguity
- When this story is complete, unit tests are written and passing for all new or modified logic

## Considerations

- [Correctness] A ticket carrying BOTH bug-type-uncategorized AND bug-type-classifier-failed-<reason> (written on failure by S2) must not double-count against both SC5(a) and SC5(c) thresholds without explicit documentation. Choose: treat classifier-failed as a strict subset of uncategorized (count once in the more specific bucket), or count separately with explicit overlap note in the labeled finding text.

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
data.title: As a DSO maintainer, I can see bug classification statistics in each retro report so that recurring bug patterns surface as explicit labeled findings
